blocks.content: The Equator represents the zero degree latitude and is the longest parallel, dividing the Earth into two equal hemispheres.

rows: Divides Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres; experiences equal day and night year-round.
Northernmost boundary of the Torrid Zone; receives vertical overhead rays of the sun during June Solstice.
Southernmost boundary of the Torrid Zone; receives vertical overhead rays of the sun during December Solstice.
Boundary of the North Frigid Zone; marks the latitude above which 24-hour daylight/darkness occurs.
Boundary of the South Frigid Zone; marks the latitude below which 24-hour daylight/darkness occurs.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Latitudes are imaginary angular distances measured north or south of the Equator from the center of the Earth.
The Equator (0°) is the largest latitude line, also called the Great Circle, which divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
All parallels of latitude are parallel to each other and decrease in circumference as they move from the Equator towards the poles.
The average distance between two consecutive degrees of latitude is approximately 111 km (69 miles).
Important parallels include the Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N), Tropic of Capricorn (23.5° S), Arctic Circle (66.5° N), and Antarctic Circle (66.5° S).
The Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N) passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.
Total number of parallels of latitude is 181 (including the Equator and both poles counted as points/lines); excluding poles, there are 179 circle parallels.
Unlike longitudes, latitude lines run parallel to each other from east to west and never intersect.
